note: Controlled relation vocabulary for claim-level nanopublications. Each relation is directional: subject -> object. An assertion uses exactly one.

reports-score.definition: the subject achieves the stated score on the named benchmark or task

outperforms.definition: the subject's measured result is better than the object's on the same benchmark

uses-method.definition: the subject's approach contains or applies the object as a component

trained-on.definition: the subject's parameters are learned from the object as training data

requires-condition.definition: the claim holds only when the object condition is satisfied
requires-condition.example: BERT fine-tuning requires-condition one extra output layer

has-limitation.definition: the object bounds the validity or scope of the subject
has-limitation.example: unidirectional LM has-limitation cannot condition on both sides

improves-on.definition: the subject is a modification that raises performance relative to the object

compared-with.definition: the subject and object are evaluated under the same conditions; no direction implied

part-of.definition: the subject is a component of the object's workflow
part-of.example: next sentence prediction part-of BERT pre-training

causes.definition: the subject is reported as the cause of the object's observed effect
causes.example: removing NSP causes lower QNLI accuracy
